title: Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA)
publisher: US Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Federal minimum wage $7.25 an hour since 24 July 2009; overtime at not less than one and one-half times the regular rate after 40 hours; no limit on hours worked per workweek for employees 16 or older.

title: Overtime Pay
publisher: US Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Time and one-half for hours over 40 in a workweek; workweek is a fixed, recurring 168-hour period that may start on any day; no averaging over two or more weeks; no premium required for weekends or holidays as such.

title: Breaks and Meal Periods
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Federal law does not require breaks; short breaks of about 5 to 20 minutes are paid work time; bona fide meal periods, typically 30 minutes or more, are not work time.

title: Fact Sheet #43: Child Labor Provisions of the FLSA for Nonagricultural Occupations
publisher: US Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Revised December 2016. 14- and 15-year-olds: 3 hours on a school day, 18 hours in a school week, 8 hours on a non-school day, 40 hours in a non-school week, 7am to 7pm (9pm from 1 June to Labor Day); no federal hours limits at 16 and over.

title: Predictive Scheduling
publisher: Oregon Bureau of Labor and Industries
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Retail, hospitality and food service employers with 500+ employees worldwide; 14 calendar days written notice; good faith estimate; one extra hour for added time or changed shifts; half rate for cut hours; time and a half within 10 hours of the previous shift unless the worker agrees; voluntary standby list rules. No page date shown.

title: Secure Scheduling Ordinance
publisher: City of Seattle, Office of Labor Standards
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Effective 1 July 2017; retail and food service with 500+ employees worldwide (full-service restaurants also 40+ locations); 14 days notice; good faith estimate; time and a half when shifts are less than 10 hours apart; predictability pay; offer hours to current staff for three days; records three years.

title: How Well is Fair Workweek Working? A Review of Existing Research (Schneider, Bruey and Harknett, 14 July 2026)
publisher: The Shift Project, Harvard Kennedy School
supports: Opened with WebFetch. San Francisco adopted the first Fair Workweek policy in 2015; 8 municipalities and 1 state since; laws reduce exposure to precarious scheduling; no conclusive evidence of reduced hours or employment; better sleep and less material hardship.

title: Stable Scheduling Increases Productivity and Sales: The Stable Scheduling Study
publisher: Center for WorkLife Law (Williams, Lambert, Kesavan and others)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Randomised study at Gap Inc., 28 stores (19 treatment, 9 control), November 2015 to August 2016; median sales +7%, labour productivity +5% ($6.20 more revenue per labour hour); only 30% of weekly payroll-hour variability explained by traffic. Report date not shown; links point to March 2018.

title: Maximum weekly working hours
supports: Opened with WebFetch. No more than 48 hours a week on average, normally over 17 weeks; opt-out possible; under 18: no more than 8 hours a day or 40 hours a week.

title: Rest breaks at work
supports: Opened with WebFetch. One uninterrupted 20-minute break when working more than 6 hours; paid or not depends on the contract; 11 hours rest between working days; 24 hours a week or 48 hours a fortnight.

title: Rest breaks at work: young workers
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Young workers: 30-minute break when working more than 4.5 hours; 12 hours daily rest; 48 hours weekly rest.

title: Night working hours
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Night period 11pm to 6am unless agreed; night worker regularly works 3 hours in it; average no more than 8 hours in 24, usually over 17 weeks; cannot opt out; 16-17 year olds not between midnight and 4am and usually not 10pm to 6am, with sector exceptions.

title: Holiday entitlement
supports: Opened with WebFetch. 5.6 weeks paid holiday, limited to 28 days; part-time pro rata; irregular-hours and part-year workers build up leave from hours worked.

title: Plan to Make Work Pay and Employment Rights Act: timeline update
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Updated 5 November 2026. Fair Work Agency from 7 April 2026; timing of the right to guaranteed hours, reasonable notice and pay for cancelled or changed shifts to follow consultation; dates may change.

title: Rates and thresholds for employers 2026 to 2027
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Updated 1 September 2026. Employer Class 1 NI 15% above the secondary threshold of £96 a week (£5,000 a year); Employment Allowance £10,500; National Minimum Wage from 1 April 2026: £12.71 (21+), £10.85 (18-20), £8 (under 18 and apprentices).

title: Employment status
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Statuses: worker, employee, self-employed and contractor, director, office holder; status affects rights and responsibilities and may differ for tax.

title: Understanding off-payroll working (IR35)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Updated 26 February 2026. In most cases the client decides status; for a small client outside the public sector the intermediary decides; the client gives a status determination statement with reasons; CEST tool.

title: Working Time Directive
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Average 48 hours a week including overtime over 4, 6 or 12 months; break after 6 hours; 11 consecutive hours daily rest; 24 hours weekly rest plus daily rest; 4 weeks paid leave; night work 8 hours average; individual opt-out with records.

title: Transparent and predictable working conditions
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Directive (EU) 2019/1152: workers told within a reasonable period in advance when work is required; measures against abuse of zero-hour contracts; probation limited to six months; applied from 1 August 2022.

title: Misclassification of Employees as Independent Contractors
publisher: US Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Final rule published 10 January 2024, effective 11 March 2024, codified at 29 CFR Part 795; no 2025 or 2026 update shown on the page.

title: Independent contractor (self-employed) or employee?
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Behavioral control, financial control and type of relationship; Form SS-8 determinations take at least six months. Last reviewed 19 May 2026.

title: Publication 15 (2026), (Circular E), Employer's Tax Guide
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Social Security 6.2% each for employer and employee, wage base $184,500; Medicare 1.45% each.

title: Employer Costs for Employee Compensation, June 2026
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Released 9 September 2026. Private industry: $46.89 per hour worked; wages and salaries $32.82 (70.0%); benefits $14.07 (30.0%).

title: Fatigue
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Higher accident and injury rates on night shifts, after a succession of shifts, on long shifts and with inadequate breaks; set, monitor and enforce limits on hours, overtime and shift swapping; overtime problems can indicate inadequate staffing; guidance HSG256.

title: Workforce planning factsheet
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Published 29 July 2025. Balancing labour supply against demand; hard and soft planning; scenario planning; six iterative stages; short-term operational staffing to long-term plans.

title: Forecasting: Principles and Practice (3rd ed.), 12.1 Complex seasonality (Hyndman and Athanasopoulos)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Hourly data usually has daily, weekly and annual seasonality; bank call volume example in 5-minute intervals; STL with multiple seasonal periods; dynamic harmonic regression with Fourier terms.

title: Erlang (unit)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Encyclopedia summary, used for the textbook definition: offered load = arrival rate times average holding time; Erlang C gives the probability of waiting and sizes call-centre staffing; assumes no abandonment, so it predicts more agents than needed.

title: Hours of work: federally regulated workplaces
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Official page on standard hours, overtime, schedule notice and rest for federally regulated employees; page date 26 August 2026. Cited as the place to check, without detail.

title: Employee records
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Some employment records kept for 7 years; rosters given to employees in advance; points to the Fair Work Ombudsman. Cited as the place to check, without detail.

title: Employees' State Insurance Corporation
publisher: ESIC, Ministry of Labour & Employment, Government of India
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Official ESIC site under the Ministry of Labour & Employment; refers to the New Labour Codes. Cited as the place to check, without detail; labour.gov.in blocked fetching (403).
